items.title: Benny Powell interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Are we talking about Barbra Streisand? Frank Sinatra or Tony Bennett? Because there is that kind of entertainer and then there’s other entertainers.

ctx.x: accountability if people are going to be paid that much money, what are they actually doing, giving back to a community? You know what I mean? And we’ll kind of pick up there. We were talking about the concept of being an artist, and how that can be consistent with, but not always the same as an entertainer. To entertain can merely mean to hold your interest. And that can be done through very positive means or very macabre or very sensational means that don’t have a lot to do with the craft of your art.

Well, when you talk about entertainers we have to sort of put in some kind of parameters. What kind of an entertainer are we talking about? Are we talking about Barbra Streisand? Frank Sinatra or Tony Bennett? Because there is that kind of entertainer and then there’s other entertainers. There’s Victor Borge and stuff. We’re still, okay, now, I think you spoke of some commitment to community as well.
